title: FCH chemoton review with a local catalyst ablation: on seed 0 a vesicle whose own K is deleted shrinks to a plain ring while its K-carrying neighbour keeps its size (individual E), but on fresh seed 5 no vesicle carries K and one K strip feeds every K-free body through the bath
summary: Re-ran the world unchanged on fresh seed 5 (fed, plus the claim's feed-cut fork at t=300) and on seed 0 (it reproduces the claim exactly: total amphiphile 4020 at t=600). I added the rubric's local ablation: at t=300, delete the catalyst K inside a disk around one body and leave u, P and every other body untouched (world_kablate.py). On seed 0, deleting K on the small vesicle shrinks it from 922 to 580 (fed twin 989) and strips it to a plain ring; deleting K on the big multilamellar vesicle shrinks it from 2688 to about 1130 (fed twin 2950). In both arms the untouched K-carrying neighbour keeps its catalyst, shape and size, and deleted K never returns. On seed 5, no vesicle carries K: K sits on one open straight strip. The K-free worms and the ring there keep a constant amphiphile mass in the fed run (e.g. 272 -> 274 from t=300 to 600), and when that strip's K is deleted every one of them, 36-120 px away, collapses to a minimal micelle (total u+1 2320 -> 122 vs 1984 in the fed twin). Amphiphile made by K is shared through the bath. A body's size therefore depends partly on its own catalyst and partly on everyone else's.

by_construction: E (amphiphile is made only by K from P and decays everywhere)
verdicts.limitation: The claimed individual, a vesicle carrying K on its bilayer, formed on 0 of 1 fresh seeds (seed 5 has an open K strip), so the claim holds on 2 of 4 seeds overall. Metabolism is partly communal: the bath carries amphiphile, so K-free rings and worms are kept alive by other bodies' catalysts (seed 5, and the K-free ring on seed 0 that holds ~600 in every arm). Locally ablated vesicles shrink to a plain ring but have not died by t=600. They may persist on the shared product, so individual E is 'loses size and structure', not death. One ablation pair on one seed; the ablation disks also remove nearby bath K (about 1000 of 4300 on seed 0). No bd twin.
